idea.title: Uber-style on-demand dog walking app, 20% commission

source.text: An Uber-style app for on-demand dog walking that takes 20% of each walk. Launch country GB, budget 5,000 GBP, 15 hours a week, goal startup, edge: I am a developer. Just go: do not ask questions.

idea.problem: Dog owners need a walker at short notice
idea.solution: An Uber-style app that matches dog owners with walkers on demand
assumptions: Price field = the 20% commission (amount 20 = percent of the walk), not a GBP price
Average walk GBP 14 (30 min), from Rover UK city price pages, 2025-09
Customer assumed: working dog owners in one UK city; not stated
Launch in one city first, since marketplace liquidity is local
No co-founder, no existing audience, no pet-care experience

confidence.note: Real CPC from Google Keyword Planner and a UK churn/leakage figure from a marketplace would raise it

gross_margin.note: Take GBP 2.80 per walk minus Stripe, vetting and guarantee reserve GBP 1.01 = 64% on net revenue

ltv_cac.note: LTV GBP 14 vs CAC GBP 83: 0.17. Walkers move repeat clients off-app, so LTV can't grow (R4 limit already met)

pricing_power.note: 20% is above Rover's 15% ad-hoc and 5% recurring fee: you would be the most expensive option

build_effort.note: Two-sided app, payments, vetting, tracking: 3-4 months at 15 h/week before a real test

skills_match.note: You can build it; supply recruitment, trust and safety, local ops are the real work and new to you

capital_needed.note: GBP 5,000 buys about 60 owners at GBP 83 CAC, before paying to recruit walkers in the same area

time_to_mvp.note: About 12 weeks to a usable two-sided app at 15 h/week (estimate)

sales_cycle.note: Owners decide in days, but want a free meet-and-greet first, as on Pawshake

channel_readiness.note: No audience; paid search costs about GBP 2.50 a click against Rover's brand (R5: no_distribution)

search_demand.note: 11.1m UK dogs and 30% of adults own one; 'dog walker' had 14,800 UK searches a month (2017)

trend.note: Flat: dog numbers fell in 2026 after the 2025 peak; walking businesses still up 29% 2023-25

willingness_to_pay.note: Owners already pay GBP 12-20 per walk on Rover and Pawshake

free_alternatives.note: BorrowMyDoggy volunteers, neighbours and family cover part of the job for little or nothing

competitor_density.note: Rover (Blackstone, USD 2.3bn), Pawshake, Tailster (30,000 carers) plus thousands of local walkers

differentiation.note: 'On-demand' is not a moat: Rover already books walks in-app, at a lower fee

legal_regulatory.note: Council PSPO dog caps and licences (Richmond GBP 141.67), insurance, and pending worker-status reform

platform_dependency.note: Apple takes no commission on walks (3.1.3(e)); the real dependency is walkers keeping clients

market_risk.note: Dogs need walking daily, but last-minute demand fell with remote work, as Wag!'s decline shows

skills.note: Developer: covers the build, not marketplace operations or pet care

assets.note: No audience, walker network or local presence stated

interest.note: No stated passion for dogs or pet care; goal is a startup

tam.reasoning: 11.1m dogs (PDSA 2025) x 1/40 use pro walkers (Dogster) = 277k dogs x 2 walks/week x 52 x GBP 14 = GBP 403m bookings x 20% take

sam.reasoning: One large city (Greater Manchester, about 3% of UK) = GBP 12m bookings x 20%

som.reasoning: 0.5% of SAM in year 1, solo founder

price.reasoning: 20% commission x GBP 14 average 30-min walk (Rover UK city pages GBP 11-15, 2025-09)

variable_cost_per_unit.reasoning: Stripe 1.5% x 14 + 0.20 = 0.41; vetting/support 0.30; guarantee and insurance reserve 0.30

expected_lifetime.reasoning: Ad-hoc owner books a few walks, then repeats go direct to the walker; Rover cut recurring fee to 5% to stop this leakage

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: Local-services search benchmark of 2-5%, mid-point 3% for a new, unknown brand

cac.reasoning: CPC GBP 2.50 (Wired Media, London) / 3% conversion = GBP 83; walker acquisition excluded

payback_months.reasoning: CAC 83 / (2 walks a month x GBP 1.79) = 23 months, longer than the owner stays

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: Hosting and maps API 25 + Apple developer 79/yr (6.6) + business insurance and tools 28 = about GBP 60

break_even_customers_per_month.unit: active owners booking 2 walks a month
break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: 60 / (2 x 1.79) = 17; excludes marketing, which is where the money goes

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: 12 weeks to build at 15 h/week + 2 weeks to recruit 10 walkers in one area

verdict.launch_reason: Stated by the user; one city first, because marketplace liquidity is local
verdict.cheapest_test: Interview 15 UK independent dog walkers and pre-sell a GBP 12/month admin tool via a landing page in 7 days
kill_criteria: Fewer than 10 of 15 walkers interviewed name admin or invoicing as a top-3 pain by day 5 -> stop
Fewer than 3 walkers pre-pay GBP 12 for month 1 by day 7 -> stop

rescue.change: Sell a scheduling, GPS-report and invoicing tool to independent UK dog walkers (GBP 12-15/month) instead of competing with them
rescue.why: Fixes strong_competitor, ltv_cac and differentiation: you serve the supply that leaves Rover, and your dev skill is the product
rescue.effort: 6-10 weeks to an MVP at 15 h/week
rescue.requires: 15 walker interviews first; check existing walker software, not researched here

rescue.change: Run a concierge recurring-walk service in one postcode: 3-5 subcontracted walkers, weekly packs, no app
rescue.why: Fixes no_distribution and time_to_mvp: leaflets, vets and local groups reach owners in days, recurring packs cut leakage
rescue.requires: Local presence, walker recruitment, worker-status-safe contracts

narrative.answer: **NO-GO** at 49/100. A 20% fee is above Rover's 15% (5% on recurring walks), each owner costs about GBP 83 to acquire and is worth about **GBP 14** before walkers take them off the app. Wag!, the US original, went bankrupt in 2025.
tldr: Rover already does on-demand walks in the UK at **15%**, and 5% on recurring care.
Unit economics are upside down: LTV:CAC about **0.17**.
Your developer skills would be better used building **tools for walkers**.

key_findings.title: You would be the most expensive platform
key_findings.detail: Rover charges UK walkers **15%** on one-off bookings and **5%** on weekly recurring care, so walkers have no reason to pay you 20%.

key_findings.title: The US original went bankrupt
key_findings.detail: Wag!, which created on-demand dog walking, filed for **Chapter 11** in 2025-07; equity was cancelled and the lender took control.

key_findings.title: Each owner costs more than they earn you
key_findings.detail: About GBP 2.50 a click and 3% conversion give a **GBP 83** CAC against about GBP 14 of lifetime contribution (estimate).

narrative.recommendation: Do not build the marketplace. Spend 7 days interviewing 15 independent UK dog walkers and pre-selling a **GBP 12/month** admin tool.
narrative.steelman: Demand is real: **11.1m dogs** in the UK and owners paying GBP 12-20 a walk. But that demand is already served by Rover at a lower fee, so the steelman supports serving walkers, not competing for owners.

premortem.cause: Owners came for one walk, then booked the same walker directly by phone, so you paid GBP 83 per owner for about GBP 14
premortem.early_signal: Under 30% of owners rebook in-app within 30 days

premortem.cause: No cheap way to reach owners: paid search against Rover burned the GBP 5,000 for about 60 owners
premortem.early_signal: CAC above GBP 50 after the first GBP 500 of ads

premortem.cause: Walkers stayed on Rover at 15% or 5% and refused 20%, so requests went unfilled
premortem.early_signal: Fewer than 10 of 50 walkers contacted sign up in 2 weeks

changes.what: Blackstone took Rover private for about USD 2.3bn, funding a leader that already owns the UK market
Rover cut its UK fee on weekly recurring care to 5% to keep repeat clients on-app
Wag!, the on-demand pioneer, filed for Chapter 11 and handed ownership to its lender
PDSA reports the UK dog population fell in 2026 after the 2025 record

why_now.note: The window closed: a funded leader, a lower fee, and the category's pioneer bankrupt.

icp.who: Working dog owners in one dense UK city who need ad-hoc midday walks
icp.pays_for_today: Rover or Pawshake walkers at GBP 12-20 per walk, or a local walker paid directly
icp.budget: About GBP 50-100 a week for daily walks (estimate: 5 x GBP 12-20)
icp.trigger: Return to the office, a new puppy, or the regular walker cancelling

customer.segment: Working dog owners in UK cities
customer.pain: No one to walk the dog midday at short notice
customer.today: Rover, Pawshake, a local walker, BorrowMyDoggy volunteers, family

use_cases.name: Concierge recurring walks in one postcode

free_alternative.evidence: BorrowMyDoggy volunteers and family cover part of the job, but not reliable on-demand walks; searched 'dog walking free UK'.

strong_competitor.evidence: Rover (Blackstone, USD 2.3bn, 2024), Pawshake, Tailster (about 30,000 UK carers) and thousands of local walkers.

graveyard.evidence: Wag! filed Chapter 11 in 2025-07 after H1 2025 revenue fell 23.8%; DogBuddy, the UK leader, was absorbed by Rover in 2018.

no_distribution.evidence: Paid search runs about GBP 2.50 a click against Rover's brand, so CAC (about GBP 83) exceeds an owner's first-year value (about GBP 14).

costs_eat_margin.evidence: Stripe 1.5% + 20p plus vetting leaves about 64% of the GBP 2.80 take; checked Stripe UK pricing.

weak_demand.evidence: 11.1m UK dogs (2025); 2026 dip is small; walking businesses grew 29% in 2023-25. Not a hit.

legal_platform_risk.evidence: Council PSPOs cap dogs per walker and require licences; Apple takes no IAP cut on walks. Compliance work, not a blocker.

saturated_wave.evidence: Searched Product Hunt 2025-11 to 2026-11: 2 dog-walk launches, both trackers (Walk with Coco, cre8pet), no marketplace clones.

competitors.traction_note: Blackstone-owned; 32,000 Trustpilot reviews, 20,640 GB App Store ratings
competitors.gap: Fees on both sides; clunky app after the Cat in a Flat merger

competitors.traction_note: About 30,000 UK carers; Pets at Home stake

competitors.name: Local independent walkers
competitors.gap: No booking tech; admin by WhatsApp

scenarios.note: 20 owners x 2 walks x GBP 2.80; GBP 800 ads + GBP 60 fixed

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.note: 60 owners x 2 walks x GBP 2.80; GBP 1,000 ads + GBP 60 fixed

scenarios.name: Optimistic
scenarios.note: 200 owners x 3 walks x GBP 2.80; GBP 1,500 ads + 60 fixed: break-even only

risks.risk: Walkers and owners move repeat bookings off-app
risks.mitigation: Recurring discount like Rover's 5%, which kills your margin

risks.risk: Incident with a dog (loss, injury, bite) on your platform
risks.mitigation: Vetting, walker insurance (from GBP 5.41/month), a guarantee fund

risks.risk: Council PSPO limits and licences vary by borough
risks.mitigation: Check the launch borough's PSPO; cap walks at 4 dogs
Walkers set their own prices and can substitute

test_plan.step: List 40 independent walkers from local Facebook groups, NARPS and Google Maps in one city
Run 15 calls of 20 minutes on how they book, invoice and report walks
test_plan.verify: 10 of 15 rank admin in their top-3 pains

test_plan.step: Put up a landing page: booking, GPS reports and invoicing for GBP 12/month
test_plan.verify: Page live, shown to the 15 walkers

test_plan.step: Ask each walker to pre-pay month 1 via a Stripe payment link
